before.overall_caption: An abstract composition from 1937 by G.L.K. Morris featuring a dynamic interplay of geometric and organic shapes in monochrome.
before.brushstroke: Visible charcoal or pencil hatching and shading create texture within the shapes, contrasting with solid black fills.
before.composition: A balanced yet active arrangement of overlapping triangles, curves, and linear elements centered on a light background.
before.color: A monochrome palette consisting of deep blacks, various shades of gray through hatching, and the off-white tone of the paper.
before.line: Bold, thick black outlines define the primary forms, complemented by thinner, sketchy lines and parallel hatching.
before.light: Even, ambient light is suggested by the white space of the paper, with no directional light source or cast shadows.

after.overall_caption: A quiet monochrome abstract drawing uses balanced curves and geometric forms to create a restrained, contemplative mood.
after.brushstroke: Soft pencil hatching and firm black strokes create gentle texture without aggressive visual pressure.
after.composition: Curved and angular shapes are spaced across the page in a balanced arrangement with ample open ground.
after.color: The limited palette of black, gray, and warm paper tones keeps the image subdued and low in intensity.
after.line: Thick black contours are offset by thin sketch lines, giving the abstraction a controlled and orderly rhythm.
after.light: Even ambient paper tone provides soft visual clarity without dramatic shadows or harsh contrast.
